From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T11:40:10-07:00
Subject: [Internal] Preliminary findings — KV cache pressure + model hot-path GC interaction

Team,

Quick summary of what we're seeing after ingesting the logs and flamegraphs:

- Root triggers: Rapid burst of long-context batched requests from TideMark's search autocomplete (spikes ~09:00). These extended sequence lengths forced increased KV cache churn.
- Observed behavior: concurrent cache compaction work led to transient high GPU memory reservations on a subset of pods; memory accounting mismatch caused the runtime to reject allocations (5xx) prior to autoscale reacting.
- Contributing factor: a recently deployed kernel selection tweak (deferred GC window) changed memory reclamation timing; under sustained burst this amplified peak usage.

Immediate actions taken (done at 09:30-10:15):
- Rolled back the deferred GC tweak on affected model family to restore prior reclamation behavior.
- Expanded the hot GPU pool by +30% to give headroom; adjusted batching to 50% of customer default for TideMark.
- Enabled prefix KV cache pinning for high-frequency routes.

Next steps for RCA write-up:
- Collect detailed allocation traces and correlate pod-level metrics with requests.
- Draft mitigations: (1) revert/adjust kernel selection heuristics permanently; (2) change autoscaler thresholds for transient cache churn; (3) provide a tailored quantization/batching recommendation to TideMark for their workload.

I'll have a draft RCA and mitigation spreadsheet ready by EOD.

- Karthik
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: ops@tidemark.com; sara.daly@tidemark.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai; vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai; lauren_bishop@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T17:05:46-07:00
Subject: TideMark incident — preliminary RCA and short-term commitments

Sara and team,

Thanks again for your patience earlier today. Attached is our preliminary RCA and an operational heatmap that explains the spike and the mitigations we applied. TL;DR:

- Cause: runtime memory accounting and GC timing interacting with KV cache churn during long-context batched bursts.
- What we did (short term): reverted GC timing tweak, scaled hot pool +30%, reduced batching on TideMark routes, enabled cache pinning. These actions restored normal error rates and latency by ~11:30 PDT.
- Short-term ETA: We recommended your front-end fall back to the lower P95 batch profile for the next 48 hours; we will keep autoscaling buffers elevated.

Commitments we are making to TideMark:
- Delivery of final RCA package and retention of full allocation traces by 2026-09-02 EOD.
- A targeted configuration profile (quantization + batching + cache settings) validated in our staging environment and a runbook for your SREs by 2026-09-03.
- A one-week operational cadence with our support lead (Marissa) and a bi-weekly health report for a month.

We apologize for the disruption. We take these incidents seriously and will deliver both technical fixes and compensatory SLA review if the impact meets the thresholds in your contract.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: TideMark_RCA_draft_v1.pdf, mitigation_plan_TideMark.xlsx
